Few developed nations routinely administer the Hepatitis B (HepB) vaccine to all newborns on the day of birth (universal birth dose within 24 hours).

- In the EU/EEA — Only five countries provide a universal birth dose: Bulgaria, Lithuania, Poland, Portugal, and Romania.
- Other high-income examples:
  - United States: Previously universal at birth, but as of December 2025, the CDC's ACIP shifted to shared decision-making for infants born to HBsAg-negative mothers (no longer universally recommended at birth).
  - Canada: No universal birth dose; starts later.
  - United Kingdom: Universal at birth (introduced more recently).
  - Australia, New Zealand, Japan, South Korea: No universal birth dose for all newborns (though some have high overall coverage starting later).
